body.target_estimand: The observed-law target is \(\theta(a)=\int m(a,w)p(w)\,dw\) for \(a\in J\). Under the frozen model this functional is not identified with \(\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y(a)]\) uniformly over full-data witnesses; an additional condition linking realized-dose consistency to deterministic-dose sections is required for that causal equality.

sampling_model.design: The observed sample is iid from \(P\in\mathcal M\). Although membership requires at least one full-data extension satisfying consistency, sectionwise conditional exchangeability, and conditional-potential-mean continuity, those conditions do not force all admissible extensions to agree on \(\mathbb E[Y(a)]\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The frozen description names boundary-corrected local-polynomial learners with bandwidth \(n^{-1/(2s)}\), but it does not yet specify a complete sample map. The advertised exponents are derived conditionally on a regular kernel, uniformly invertible boundary moment system, normalization map, and singular-matrix convention; the centered validation-fold V-statistic bound remains open.
sampling_model.overlap: The conditional density \(g(a\mid w)\) is bounded above and away from zero.
sampling_model.treatment: Continuous dose \(A_i\in[0,1]\), with inference restricted to \(J=[\delta,1-\delta]\).
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(W_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with compact covariates and bounded outcomes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The limiting distribution is the integral of the difference of the squared constrained and unconstrained slope processes.
We study the extremal behavior of the stationary argmax process on increasing intervals.
A suitably standardized supremum of the Grenander-type estimation error converges to a standard Gumbel random variable.
The confidence intervals concern the continuous treatment effect curve at a fixed point and invert a likelihood-ratio-type test.
The paper provides general conditions for consistency and pointwise convergence of generalized Grenander-type estimators.
Approximation results for the supremum of an empirical process yield asymptotically valid uniform confidence bands.
The paper develops a bootstrap procedure for constructing uniform confidence bands from weighted local-linear estimation.

body.tldr: The frozen assumptions do not identify an exact-dose causal curve: an explicit pair of admissible full-data extensions has the same observed law but causal means differing at every dose. The Brownian--GCM extreme-value program also remains open at its load-bearing step: exact scaling and a finite-action plateau witness are available, but no sharp cluster-intensity expansion, additive tail ratio, Poisson limit, or growing-domain transfer has been proved. Consequently the current construction defines an observed-law isotonic LR profile and a proposed calibration architecture, not a validated simultaneous causal confidence procedure.

project_justification.gap: The literature supplies fixed-dose Brownian--GCM LR limits and neighboring extreme-value results for different shape-constrained functionals, but the sharp high-excursion cluster law for the LR energy field is not established here. Separately, the frozen sectionwise exchangeability and continuity conditions leave a random-diagonal nonidentification gap for exact continuous doses.
project_justification.niche: A valid contribution would require both a repaired exact-dose causal bridge and a sharp growing-domain LR excursion theorem, followed by a uniform primitive-to-LR transfer. The current round identifies these as distinct mathematical bottlenecks.
project_justification.fill: This round proves a two-extension nonidentification witness, the nuisance-rate exponents for a fully specified regular boundary local-polynomial implementation, three numerical transfer clauses, the canonical stationarity identity, an exact small-noise scaling and action bracket, the spatial-volume clock algebra, feasible-centering calculus conditional on upstream limits, and deterministic profile inversion. It does not claim that the unresolved excursion, transfer, or coverage theorems are established.

body.related_work: Banerjee and Wellner (2001) provide the one-location Brownian--GCM LR law, not the growing-domain cluster expansion claimed by the open canonical theorem. Hooghiemstra and Lopuhaä (1998) and Durot, Kulikov, and Lopuhaä (2012) concern extremes of related argmax or slope-error processes and do not establish the LR-energy tail used here. Westling, Gilbert, and Carone (2020), Westling and Carone (2020), and Doss (2026) motivate causal-isotonic primitives and pointwise inference, but no result cited in this core repairs the explicit random-diagonal witness under the frozen assumptions. Takatsu and Westling (2025), Ai, Huang, and Zhang (2026), and the Doss--VandenBerg multiscale work remain neighboring simultaneous-band approaches; no optimal-width, tuning-freedom, or dominance claim is made.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact Brownian scaling reduces the one-point tail to a small-noise GCM-energy event, and the explicit plateau gives the action bracket \(1/2\le I_\star\le9/8\). These facts do not determine the sharp tail prefactor, additive ratio, declustered intensity, anticlustering, Poisson law, or grid approximation. On the statistical side, the frozen learner is not a complete sample map, the validation-fold empirical term requires a conditional V-statistic decomposition, and optimized LR stability requires common contact localization and slope control.
body.honest_scope: No simultaneous causal band theorem is proved under the frozen core. Exact-dose identification is refuted by two admissible extensions of the same observed law; a future repair must add or reformulate a genuine bridge between realized-dose consistency and deterministic-dose sections. The canonical excursion theorem, growing-domain oracle coupling, cross-fitted optimized-value transfer, random-horizon simulation approximation, and nominal coverage remain open. The proved components are the explicit nonidentification witness, conditional learner-rate algebra, three transfer remainder orders, finite-dimensional stationarity, small-noise scaling and action bracket, the spatial clock, conditional centering calculus, deterministic profile inversion, and homogeneous reduction. No claim is made about optimal width, tuning freedom, or dominance over Doss--VandenBerg multiscale Gaussian bands.
body.interpretation: With the frozen assumptions, \(\theta(a)=\int m(a,w)p(w)\,dw\) is an observed-law G-computation curve. It cannot yet be interpreted uniformly as the exact-dose causal mean across admissible full-data extensions. Likewise, the displayed LR bands and threshold-crossing image are algorithmic objects whose nominal simultaneous coverage is conditional on unresolved canonical and transfer theorems.
